https://www.politico.eu/article/swiss-re.text: Swiss voters appear to have rejected a proposal to introduce a more rigid enforcement of the country's neutrality principle — repudiating an idea which would have made imposing sanctions against Moscow more difficult. In a referendum which took place Sunday, around 7 out of 10 Swiss participants voted against the "safeguard Swiss neutrality" initiative, according to projections from the Swiss polling institute GFS Bern. Early official results put the "no" camp at 68%, with a participation rate of 46%. Counting is still in progress. If the proposal had been approved, Switzerland's neutrality, enshrined in the Constitution since 1848, would have been interpreted more strictly, with the country not joining or participating in any military or security alliance, and not imposing sanctions on hostile states. Advertisement Advertisement There were concerns that a “yes” vote would have effectively prevented Switzerland from imposing sanctions on Russia — unless they were approved by the United Nations Security Council, where Moscow has veto power. Russia openly backed the initiative, which was introduced by the right-wing Pro Switzerland organization. Pro Swizerland argued that Swiss neutrality should always be applied and "not adjusted on a case-by-case or ad hoc basis." Switzerland has largely mirrored the EU's sanctions against Moscow. The country expanded its sanctions list in mid-August, following the EU's 20th sanctions package. Both the Swiss government and the Swiss Parliament had advised rejecting the proposal. Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis, who leads the country's foreign affairs department, had said that the country's current neutrality regime "has proved its worth." Swiss voters face another neutrality question later this year. In November, they will be asked to assess whether Switzerland's arms export rules are still fit for purpose or whether the country should be allowed to export weapons to a defined group of 25 mostly Western countries, even if they are involved in an ongoing conflict. If approved, that change would tighten Swiss ties with Western countries and could boost its defense industry's export earnings. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teess.text: A stepfather accused of murdering a student he was sexually obsessed with downloaded hundreds of sexual images of her in the weeks leading up to her death, a court has heard. Nathan Owens, 34, from Hartlepool, is accused of attacking Carla Georgescu with a sharp object and strangling her at her university halls of residence in Preston. Carla was discovered suspended from a wardrobe by a belt after her mother contacted campus security when she was unable to reach her on her 20th birthday, February 5, 2026. Owens, Carla's stepfather, visited her at 4.30am on February 4, and is said by the prosecution to have been the last person to see her alive. He denies murder, GBH and strangulation. Prosecutors allege he killed her as the culmination of a sexual obsession - potentially driven by jealousy upon discovering she intended to meet her online boyfriend in Romania for the first time. The jury at Preston Crown Court heard evidence from Dominic Kirby, a police digital media investigator, who examined Owens' laptop following Carla's death on February 5, 2026. He found that 14,417 still and moving images had been transferred to the HP device between January 23 and 24 — a fortnight before Carla died, reports Lancs Live . The jury was told that the majority of the images were pornographic in nature and depicted adult females. Among the evidence were hundreds of covert photographs taken of Carla at the family home, in which she was dressed in underwear or short pyjamas. The jury was shown a selection of images that the prosecution claims were captured by Owens as he sat on the sofa, unbeknownst to Carla. The images depict her carrying out everyday household tasks such as emptying bins or folding laundry, while dressed in knickers and vest tops, or pyjamas. Nicholas Lumley KC said: "It is the prosecution case that Carla had no idea these were being taken. There are a number of covert images taken by the defendant and some of them had been viewed in the days leading up to his visit to Preston." The prosecution also alleges that Owens manipulated pornographic images by superimposing Carla's face onto explicit photographs of naked women. "Time and again, Carla's face is superimposed onto pornographic images," the prosecutor said. Additionally, a video and 30 screenshots allegedly showed Owens engaging in a sex act with an effigy dressed in Carla's clothing. The effigy's head was an anime doll belonging to Carla, which Owens was seen with in a series of still images. The jury was also shown a photograph of Owens wearing Carla's nightie, which the prosecution contends he viewed prior to visiting the student in the early hours of February 4, 2026. Owens, of Hopps Street, Hartlepool, denies murder, strangulation and GBH at Preston Crown Court.
